name: apple-music-mcp
description: Search your music library and read its play history, through the Music app
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Music app on this Mac.

Music has no framework a separate process can use, so this server drives Music.app itself through Apple events. Music must be running, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

The interesting part is what Music already records and rarely shows you: play counts, last played, skip counts, ratings, date added. Those come back as raw rows. This server computes no statistics and ranks nothing — the reading of the rows is Claude's job, where you can see it happen and argue with it.

Nothing here removes a track or a playlist. add_to_playlist only ever appends, and refuses smart playlists, whose contents are the output of their rules. Because there is no way back, it takes a skip_duplicates option for the case that actually bites: retrying an add that had already gone through.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: music_status
tools.description: Reports whether Music is running and whether this server may drive it, and says exactly what to enable and where if it may not. Also shows the scan and result limits this server is configured…

tools.name: now_playing
tools.description: Returns the current track with its full library row, how far into it playback has reached, the player state, the volume, and the playlist it is coming from.

tools.name: music_search
tools.description: Finds tracks, albums, artists or playlists whose text matches a query. Returns one line each, with the id needed by track_get, playlist_get or add_to_playlist.

tools.name: tracks_list
tools.description: Returns library rows with every field Music stores about a track except the lyrics: play count and last played, skip count and last skipped, rating, favourite and dislike flags, date added, genre,…

tools.name: playlists_list
tools.description: Lists every playlist with its id, track count, total time, and whether add_to_playlist can append to it.

tools.name: playlist_get
tools.description: Returns a playlist's details and its tracks as raw rows, the same shape tracks_list returns.

tools.name: track_get
tools.description: Returns everything Music stores about one or more tracks, including the lyrics — the one field tracks_list leaves out, because reading it costs a round trip per track.

tools.name: create_playlist
tools.description: Creates a new, empty playlist in Music.

tools.name: add_to_playlist
tools.description: Appends tracks to an existing playlist. It only ever adds: nothing already in the playlist is removed, replaced or reordered. Pass skip_duplicates=true to leave out ids the playlist already holds — worth setting when retrying an add that may already have succeeded.

tools.name: music_control
tools.description: CHANGES WHAT IS CURRENTLY PLAYING on this Mac: starts or pauses playback, skips to the next or previous track, or sets the system music volume. The effect is immediate and audible to whoever is at…
